subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin-facing config pre-apply veto for all persisted config mutations, and what ordering, metadata, and failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: This creates a public plugin API around security-sensitive persisted config writes, so code inspection cannot choose the product/security contract on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Design guarded pre-apply hook
options.body: Add a documented hook after built-in validation and SecretRef preflight but before persistence, covering gateway RPC and shared mutation helpers with typed rejection and no-write tests.

options.title: Keep built-in validation only
options.body: Reject the new hook for now and rely on allowlisted config RPC writes, schema validation, SecretRef preflight, doctor, and explicit wrapper workflows.

recommendation.title: Design guarded pre-apply hook
recommendation.body: Add a documented hook after built-in validation and SecretRef preflight but before persistence, covering gateway RPC and shared mutation helpers with typed rejection and no-write tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They already framed this issue as an open config validation/mutation API decision and have adjacent config/runtime history.
